writeup.headline: Coinbase rates Sell on shrinking revenue and a weak share-price trend, with Q3 results due after today's close.
writeup.thesis: Coinbase scores 39, a Sell, driven mainly by weak growth (25) and a very weak trend score (9). Revenue is shrinking, with a TTM revenue decline of 10.3% and a latest-quarter revenue decline of 18.5% year on year, though growth sped up by 12.0 pp from the previous quarter. The shares are price 54.3% below its 52-week high and down 47.4% from 12 months ago to 1 month ago, trailing both SPY and QQQ. Quality (56) and news risk (64) partly offset this: operating margin is 9.9% and the diluted share count is down 5.6% year on year, while recent news includes a dismissed investor class action, supportive stablecoin rules and incremental product launches. Valuation and balance sheet could not be scored; in absolute terms P/S of 6.8x and EV/EBIT of 65.2x are high, and P/S sits near the middle of the last 57 month-ends (cheaper than at 35, more expensive than at 21).
key_risks: Revenue keeps falling, with a latest-quarter decline of 18.5% year on year tied to crypto trading activity
Q3 results after today's close could disappoint against July guidance
Weak price momentum: price 10.0% below its 50-day average and 9.4% below its 200-day average
Absolute valuation is high at 65.2x EV/EBIT despite shrinking sales
Stock-based compensation at 14.9% of revenue and competition such as Webull's planned perpetual futures launch
what_would_change: A 6-point score gain would lift the rating to Hold, most likely via a return to revenue growth improving the growth score
A recovery in the share price relative to its moving averages and to SPY/QQQ would raise the very low trend score
A 10-point score drop would push it to Strong Sell, for example from a weak Q3 report, guidance cut or adverse regulatory news
Margin compression in Q3 that pulls down the quality score would add downside pressure
